title: IMF Executive Board approves a 15.6 billion dollar Extended Fund Facility for Ukraine
body:
On 31 March 2023 the Executive Board of the International Monetary Fund approved a 48-month Extended Fund Facility arrangement for Ukraine of SDR 11.6 billion, about 15.6 billion US dollars or 577 percent of quota. About SDR 2 billion, or 2.7 billion dollars, was available for immediate disbursement. The arrangement was one component of a 115 billion dollar international support package.

The programme was designed in two phases. In the first, covering 2023 and 2024 during the war, Ukraine committed to adopt a robust 2023 budget, raise revenue without measures that erode the tax base, keep disinflation steady, keep the exchange rate stable with adequate reserves, assess banking sector health, protect social spending and advance governance and anti-corruption reforms. In the second phase, after active combat subsides, it would return to a flexible exchange rate and inflation targeting and pursue structural reforms and public investment management for reconstruction.

Creditors agreed to a two-step debt treatment: extending the debt standstill, which then expired at the end of December 2023, by three years, and carrying out a final debt treatment before the arrangement expired. The IMF press release gave real GDP growth of 3.4 percent in 2021 and minus 30.3 percent in 2022, with a projection between minus 3 percent and plus 1 percent for 2023, and public debt rising from 50.4 percent of GDP in 2021 to 81.7 percent in 2022.
